q: Is rail freight lower carbon than trucking in India, and by how much per tonne-km?
title: Rail vs road freight emissions in India
short: Yes. On GLEC Framework defaults, diesel rail freight is about 0.022 kg CO2e per tonne-km against about 0.062 for a large articulated truck, roughly 65 percent lower. Door to door the gap narrows, because rail needs road legs at each end and often a longer route.
audience: Indian manufacturers and exporters moving goods to ports

ul: Articulated truck over 17 t, around 70 percent loaded: about 0.062 kg CO2e per tonne-km.
Rigid truck of 7.5 to 17 t, around 55 percent loaded: about 0.182 kg CO2e per tonne-km, nearly three times the large truck.
Diesel rail freight: about 0.022 kg CO2e per tonne-km.
Electric rail freight: about 0.010 kg CO2e per tonne-km on the GLEC default, which depends on the grid behind it.
p: These are well-to-wheel defaults as used in Senseible's logistics calculator, labelled GLEC v3.0. Check them against the current GLEC tables before you report.

Most Indian freight trains now run on electric traction, and India's grid is coal heavy at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. A default built on a cleaner grid can understate an Indian electric train. To build an India figure, take traction energy and net tonne-km from the latest Indian Railways Year Book: kWh per net tonne-km x 0.710 for electric, litres per net tonne-km x 2.68 for diesel. Label the result as your estimate and show it next to the GLEC default.

sections.h: Why door to door matters more than the mode factor
ul: Road legs from the factory to the rail siding or ICD, and from the railhead onward, carry the truck factor and can be a large share of the total on a short rail haul.
Rail distance between two points is often longer than the road distance; use each mode's real distance.
Container handling at the ICD and port adds emissions that a direct truck avoids.
On hauls under a few hundred kilometres, the road legs can cancel most of the rail advantage. On long hauls to Mundra, JNPA or Chennai, rail usually wins clearly.

p: Compare the full chain, both options on the same well-to-wheel basis and the same cargo weight. If rail plus road legs comes out lower and the transit time works, switch, and keep the railway receipt and the road lorry receipts so each leg can be shown.

example.title: Worked example: 20 t to the port, road against rail
lines: All road, 1,200 km by articulated truck: 20 x 1,200 = 24,000 tonne-km x 0.062 = 1,488 kg CO2e
Rail option, road leg to ICD: 20 x 40 = 800 tonne-km x 0.062 = 49.6 kg CO2e
Rail option, diesel rail 1,300 km: 20 x 1,300 = 26,000 tonne-km x 0.022 = 572 kg CO2e
Rail option total: 49.6 + 572 = 621.6 kg CO2e, about 58 percent below all road
Terminal handling at the ICD and port is extra on the rail option; add it from terminal or GLEC hub data
example.note: Distances are illustrative. Diesel rail is used as a cautious choice; an India-specific electric figure may differ.

senseible: Senseible reads freight records and applies weight x distance x the mode factor; a record without weight or distance gets no figure and is marked as needing data. Its logistics calculator compares modes leg by leg on GLEC defaults, but it holds no Indian Railways traction data.
